doc.tool: Current state with the head, left wrist and right wrist images.

doc.code:
Both arms' end-effector poses (env frame), joints and grippers; success and step count (the partial-credit score is the evaluator's).

Example:
    st = state()
    print(st["arms"]["left"]["tcp_pos"], st["arms"]["right"]["gripper"], st["env_steps"])

quat_wxyz.description: [qw, qx, qy, qz] (default: keep the orientation)

return_frames.description: Also return head frames along the motion

doc.tool: Move one arm's gripper in a straight line to an env-frame [x, y, z] in metres (+x toward the robot's right, +y away from the robot, +z up; the table top is z = 0.74; at most {{max_move}} m from where it is), optionally with a [qw, qx, qy, qz] orientation (default: keep it), after an optional gripper command. The other arm holds still. Stops at the first unreachable waypoint (`stopped`). Returns the new state and images.
doc.code:
Move one arm's end effector in a straight line to an env-frame xyz (m, at most 0.5 m away) and optional wxyz orientation; the other arm holds.

Example:
    r = move_to("left", [-0.3, -0.2, 0.9], gripper=1)  # open, then go
    print(r["final_error_m"], r.get("stopped"))

return_frames.description: Also return head frames along the motion

doc.tool: Translate one arm's gripper by an env-frame [dx, dy, dz] in metres (at most {{max_move}} m per call), orientation held, after an optional gripper command. Returns the new state and images.
doc.code:
Translate one arm's end effector by an env-frame delta (m, at most 0.5 per call), orientation held.

Example:
    r = move_delta("right", [0, 0, -0.05])  # down 5 cm
    print(r["moved_m"], r["arms"]["right"]["tcp_pos"])

yaw.description: rad about env +z (+ counter-clockwise seen from above)

return_frames.description: Also return head frames along the motion

doc.tool: Turn one arm's gripper by `yaw` radians about the vertical through it (+ counter-clockwise seen from above; at most {{max_rotate}} rad per call), holding its position. Returns the new state and images.
doc.code:
Turn one arm's gripper by a yaw (rad, + counter-clockwise seen from above; clipped to 0.8) about the vertical through it.

Example:
    r = rotate_delta("left", 0.3)
    print(r["yaw"], r.get("clipped"))

return_frames.description: Also return head frames along the motion

doc.tool: Move one gripper to `value`: 1 fully open .. 0 fully closed. Returns the new state and images.
doc.code:
Move one gripper to a value, 1 open .. 0 closed.

Example:
    set_gripper("right", 0.0)  # close the right gripper

return_frames.description: Also return head frames along the motion

doc.tool: Drive both arms back to their start pose (grippers unchanged). Most tasks count as done only once both arms are back home with the grippers open.
doc.code:
Drive both arms back to their start joints (most tasks require it for success).

Example:
    r = go_home()
    print(r["success"], r["ended"])

pixels.description: [[col, row], ...] of the latest head image

camera_name.description: Only the head camera has depth (default head)

doc.tool: Env-frame [x, y, z] (m) of [col, row] pixels of the latest head image, from its depth. Read-only.
doc.code:
Env-frame xyz of [col, row] pixels of the latest head image, from its metric depth. Returns {frame, xyz: [[x, y, z] or None, ...]}.

Example:
    r = back_project([[320, 240]])
    print(r["xyz"][0])

Solve inverse kinematics for one arm's end effector (RoboDojo's cuRobo IK, from the arm's current joints); raises when there is no solution.

Returns:
    joints: 6 joint angles, rad.

Example:
    q = solve_ik([-0.3, -0.2, 0.9], [0, 1, 0, 0], "left")
    move_to_joints(q, "left")

return_frames.description: Also return head frames along the motion

doc.code:
Move one arm to a joint configuration, interpolating in joint space (at most 0.05 rad per joint per control step); the other arm holds. Returns the motion report with final_joint_error_rad.

Example:
    r = move_to_joints(solve_ik([-0.3, -0.2, 0.9], [0, 1, 0, 0], "left"), "left")
    print(r["final_joint_error_rad"], r["arms"]["left"]["tcp_pos"])

start_pose_wxyz_xyz.description: Start pose: wxyz then xyz; the arm's current end-effector pose (within 1 cm / 0.05 rad)

doc.code:
Plan joint waypoints [N, 6] (N <= 100) from the arm's current pose to another (RoboDojo's cuRobo motion planner; without one, IK along a straight line). Nothing moves; raises when no path is found.

Example:
    st = state()["arms"]["left"]
    start = list(st["eef_quat_wxyz"]) + list(st["eef_pos"])
    traj = traj_plan(start, [0, 1, 0, 0, -0.3, -0.2, 0.9], "left")
    move_along_trajectory(traj, "left")

return_frames.description: Also return head frames along the motion

doc.code:
Move one arm through joint-space waypoints in order (a waypoint farther than 0.05 rad per joint is interpolated); stops on stop or at the episode's end.

Example:
    r = move_along_trajectory(traj, "left")
    print(r["executed"], r["final_joint_error_rad"])

depth.description: The head's [rgb, depth_m] (the wrists have no depth)

doc.code:
The latest frame of 'head', 'left_wrist' or 'right_wrist'.

Example:
    rgb = render_camera("head")  # uint8 [H, W, 3]

camera_name.description: Only the head camera is calibrated

doc.code:
The head camera's OpenCV intrinsics and camera-to-env extrinsic.

Example:
    meta = get_camera_meta("head")
    K, T = meta["intrinsic_K"], meta["extrinsic_cam2world"]

RoboDojo's native observation dict (vision, state, action, instruction).

Example:
    obs = get_obs()
    print(obs["state"].keys(), obs["instruction"])

One native RoboDojo action dict (left/right_arm_joint_state 6 + left/right_ee_joint_state 1, or left/right_ee_pose 7) = one 25 Hz control step.

Example:
    q = state()["arms"]["left"]["joints_command"]
    r = step({"left_arm_joint_state": list(q), "left_ee_joint_state": [0.0]})  # close left
    print(r["terminated"], r["state"]["arms"]["left"]["gripper"])

Native RoboDojo action dicts in order, in one call.

Example:
    r = chunk_step([{"right_ee_joint_state": [1.0]}] * 8)  # open right, 8 control steps
    print(r["info"]["executed"], r["terminated"])
